issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry strips every LoggingHandler from the root logger as a global side effect.
issues.detail: The deadlock workaround removes all opentelemetry LoggingHandler instances from the root logger, not just the one this module installed. Any user- or library-installed OTLP handler gets ripped out without consent. Hold a reference to the handler created in _setup_cloud_tracer and detach only that one; document the frame explicitly.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer locates the OTLP handler by isinstance scan of root.handlers instead of holding a reference.
issues.detail: Replay picks the first LoggingHandler found on the root logger and silently no-ops if none match or if a different OTLP handler is encountered first. Since _setup_cloud_tracer knows which handler it installed, store and address it by identity. Otherwise the crash-log upload path — the very behavior this PR fixes — fails silently again.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler holds an unbounded list of LogRecord with no cap, drop policy, or time bound.
issues.detail: Between _on_setup and either init_recording or _on_cleanup, the buffer grows without limit. A slow hang or a chatty library at DEBUG can OOM the worker before the crash-log feature ever fires. Use a bounded ring (deque with maxlen, or byte budget) and define drop-oldest semantics; log a count when records are dropped.

issues.description: PR bundles unrelated changes: makefile -n auto removal, dropped test_plugin_google_stt, worker.py reorder.
issues.detail: The worker.py reorder of pending-assignment registration before _queue_msg is a real race fix; the makefile changes serialize CI and silently drop a plugin test. None relate to crash-log upload. Split into separate commits with stated rationale so bisect, revert, and review work per concern.

issues.description: init_recording is overloaded — called from _on_cleanup with synthetic RecordingOptions to opportunistically flush crash logs.
issues.detail: init_recording's precondition was clean (not initialized, cloud URL); it now also handles early-return teardown of buffering on the wrong-state path. Split into a dedicated _ensure_crash_log_pipeline (or explicit teardown) so the contract and preconditions are visible and don't drift.

issues.description: _on_entry_done overloads _shutdown_fut to carry crash signaling alongside orderly shutdown semantics.
issues.detail: Forcing _shutdown_fut.set_result with reason='job crashed' conflates two distinct postconditions on one future. Downstream consumers previously could assume orderly shutdown; now the same channel carries crash. Use a typed reason (CRASH vs USER vs TIMEOUT) and have consumers branch, or use a separate signal.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR addresses a real defect — crash logs lost when sessions fail to start — and the overall shape (buffer early, replay through OTLP, force-resolve shutdown on crash) is correct. But the implementation leaks across module boundaries: _shutdown_telemetry mutates global root-logger state, replay finds its OTLP sink by isinstance scan instead of by reference, and the buffer is unbounded. init_recording is overloaded for a cleanup-time use, and _shutdown_fut now carries crash signaling. The diff also bundles unrelated worker.py, makefile, and test changes. NEEDS-WORK: scope handler ownership by reference, bound the buffer, split unrelated changes.
